title: Home Purchase Agreement Terms for a Buyer Holding a Second Open Agreement
content:
**Section 1. Second open agreement.** Where the buyer already has another open Home Purchase Agreement (at least one other agreement in status pending ratification, ratified, under construction or closing scheduled) when a new agreement is written:

(a) the new agreement may not carry a home-sale contingency;

(b) the initial earnest money of the new agreement is raised by 5.0 percent of its contract price, rounded half up to the cent, and that amount is posted as a concurrent agreement deposit on top of every other deposit component of the new agreement.

**Section 2. One incentive agreement.** Only one open agreement per buyer may carry builder incentives: incentives are granted on the earlier-dated agreement and not on the later one. The earlier-dated agreement is the one with the earlier contract date, read from Calloway's agreement records for the same buyer together with each agreement's status and the incentives already granted on the agreement ledger.

**Section 3. Worked illustration (hypothetical figures).** A buyer holds one agreement under construction and signs a second agreement at a hypothetical contract price of 412345.67.

1. The other open agreement means Section 1 applies to the second agreement.
2. The concurrent agreement deposit is 5.0 percent of 412345.67, which is 20617.2835, rounded half up to the cent: 20617.28.
3. That 20617.28 posts as its own deposit component, in addition to the initial earnest money and every other component the second agreement carries.
4. The second agreement is written without a home-sale contingency.
5. Builder incentives may be carried by only one of the two open agreements: the earlier-dated one (here the agreement under construction, being the earlier contract date); the second agreement is not granted incentives.

**Section 4. Questions on these terms.**

*Does the concurrent agreement deposit replace the initial earnest money?* No. It is posted on top of every other component.

*What is the percentage applied to?* The contract price of the new agreement, that is its base price plus its lot premium.
